anatomy.flutter: native_select.dart's own doc comment: 'This component is split in two, and only one half is a port: the closed control — 1:1, measured... the open list — DIVERGENT. The port mounts its own SelectMenu — SelectContent's surface, rows, tick and keyboard — where the OS would have drawn its picker.' NativeSelect builds a Surface(control) wrapped in Popover(content: SelectMenu<T>).
anatomy.web: native-select.tsx renders a real <select data-slot="native-select"> with <NativeSelectOption>/<NativeSelectOptGroup> children styled bg-[Canvas] text-[CanvasText] so the operating system itself draws the open option list — there is no JS-driven menu component on the web side at all.
anatomy.note: This is exactly the documented, deliberate divergence the Dart file states up front ('ruling L6, option c'): a real OS-drawn <select> has no Flutter equivalent, so Flutter substitutes its own SelectMenu (borrowed from select.dart) for the open list while keeping the closed control 1:1. This is the correct platform answer and is recorded as platform-difference rather than gap, per the source's own framing.

api.flutter: NativeSelect<T>({options, value, onChanged, size=NativeSelectSize.md, enabled=true, disabledReason, invalid=false, expand=false, width, focusNode, label, hint}); NativeSelectSize enum {sm, md} maps to data-[size=sm]/data-[size=default].
api.web: NativeSelectProps = Omit<ComponentProps<"select">, "size"> & {size?: "sm"|"default"} — a real <select> with all native HTML select attributes (value, onChange, disabled, required, etc.) plus the same size="sm"|"default" variant axis the Dart enum's .label getter produces.

states.flutter: NativeSelectSize.height getter returns space(8)=32px for md and space(7)=28px for sm, transcribed from a doc-comment table stating the control class is `h-8` ('height | 32px (h-8) — the Select beside it is 40. selects-map drift 8') with `data-[size=sm]:h-7` (28px).
states.web: The current native-select.tsx control className reads `min-h-10 w-full min-w-0 ... data-[size=sm]:min-h-8 ...` — min-h-10 is 40px and data-[size=sm]:min-h-8 is 32px, not the h-8 (32px) / data-[size=sm]:h-7 (28px) the Dart doc comment quotes verbatim at 'native-select.tsx:19, :28, :31, :43'.
states.note: Reclassified on review from `gap`: the shortfall recorded below is on the FLUTTER side — the web has the capability, or Flutter's own doc comment records it as not ported, or Flutter reproduces an earlier state of the web source that has since moved on. This ledger measures the web's convergence onto Flutter's vocabulary, so it is a pass here. The worker's original finding is kept verbatim after this line, because the finding is still true and still worth a Flutter reader's attention. ORIGINAL: The web source has changed since the Flutter file's doc comment was written: it now uses min-h-10/min-h-8 (a floor, not a fixed height) instead of h-8/h-7, and the actual pixel values have grown by 8px at both rungs (32→40 for default, 28→32 for sm). This directly contradicts the doc comment's own framing that NativeSelect at 32px is smaller than Select's 40px ('the Select beside it is 40. selects-map drift 8') — the two controls may now be the same height. NativeSelectSize.height, .radius and the Dart Padding/SizedBox built from it are stale relative to the current web markup and need re-measuring.

disabled.flutter: NativeSelect.enabled combines with FieldScope via _fieldEnabled/_enabled; Disabled(disabled: !_fieldEnabled, reason: widget.disabledReason ?? _scope?.disabledReason) wraps the control, and doc comment states 'the dim is opacity-50 on the wrapper, not on the control' — IgnorePointer only stops pointers while Disabled paints the dim on the outer Surface/wrapper.
disabled.web: The wrapper div carries `group/native-select relative w-fit has-[select:disabled]:opacity-50` — the dim is on the wrapper via the :has() selector reading the inner <select disabled>, exactly matching the Dart comment's 'the dim is opacity-50 on the wrapper, not on the control,' and the <select> itself carries disabled:pointer-events-none disabled:cursor-not-allowed.

interaction.flutter: _onKey documents the platform-authentic keyboard split: 'a closed <select> walks its own value with the arrow keys without opening anything... Enter, Space and Alt+Down open it; Home and End jump; Escape closes without committing.' _step() moves the value directly and does not wrap ('they do not wrap — a <select> on its last option stays there'); _move() inside the open SelectMenu does wrap.
interaction.web: The web control is a native <select> element, so this exact keyboard model (closed-state arrow-walks-value, Enter/Space/Alt+Down/F4 opens, Home/End jump, Escape cancels) is supplied by the operating system itself rather than any JS in native-select.tsx — the doc comment explicitly calls this out as 'the one behaviour that would be a real regression to lose,' and the Dart port reimplements it keystroke-for-keystroke to match native <select> behavior.

semantics.flutter: NativeSelect wraps its control in Semantics(button: true, label: widget.label ?? _scope?.label, hint: widget.hint ?? _scope?.describedBy, value: shown?.label, expanded: _open, enabled: _enabled) — publishing name, hint, current value text and open/closed state to the accessibility tree.
semantics.web: A native <select> automatically exposes an accessible role, its current selected option's text as the accessible value, and an expanded/collapsed state to the OS accessibility API, associated to a <label for="..."> the doc comment notes supplies 'Country' on the page; there is no bespoke ARIA needed because it is a real form control.
